summary: node1 now serves the exact response `secure-os-comparison-ready` at https://10.100.15.10:8443/ using a system-trusted certificate. The service and firewall configuration persisted across a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Generated a local CA and CA-signed server certificate with node1 DNS and IP SANs.
Added the CA to the RHEL system trust store.
Configured an unprivileged, systemd-managed HTTPS web service.
Opened TCP 8443 in runtime and persistent firewalld configuration.
Restarted node1 safely and verified full recovery.

evidence.requirement: HTTPS on TCP 8443 returns the exact required content
evidence.summary: Direct HTTPS requests to the managed-node IP returned HTTP 200 with the exact body; port 8443 was listening before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Certificate is trusted by the system
evidence.summary: The certificate includes DNS:node1 and IP:10.100.15.10, verifies against RHEL's system CA bundle, and ordinary curl requests succeed without disabling certificate validation.
secure-web.service is enabled and active; firewalld permits 8443 at runtime and permanently, including after restart.

Healthy baseline used boot ID bdbfa15c-cfc4-4b36-8edd-d0a49076e9c5; reboot was acknowledged before disconnect; execution returned with boot ID efc6fe44-d7ef-429f-b2b8-8ad47337b071; service, listener, firewall, certificate trust, and exact HTTPS response all recovered.
